roles.name: Semantic State, Provenance, and Flow Architecture
roles.lens: Focus on concerns A and B as one shared semantic-state problem. Use evidence from lyra-compiler/src/main/java/io/mindspice/lyra/compiler/semantic/SemanticResolver.java, TypeChecker.java, TypedSemanticProvenance.java, TypedSemanticGraph.java, related types, and Domain11SemanticTest.java. Trace where aggregate identity, exact selector paths, binding-local mutation, callable candidates, captured mutable cells, source-position visibility, branch/coalesce joins, and reassignment state are represented or recomputed. Determine whether the four semantic components are independently modeling a hidden abstract interpreter, and compare the current-map/set patch strategy, a shared immutable semantic value/provenance algebra with transfer functions, and one bounded flow/effect interpreter, including migration risk and API boundaries. Require evidence-backed symbols and tests, explicit invariants for sibling non-taint and any-reachable-path rejection, inputs/outputs and ownership for assignable subdomains, non-overlapping file ownership, and a gate that can stop counterexample whack-a-mole without changing language semantics. Do not implement code or make a final decision for the overall brainstorm.

roles.name: Eager Evaluation, Higher-Order Dependencies, and Cycle Architecture
roles.lens: Focus on concern C and the initialization-specific interface to the shared semantic state. Inspect InitializationAnalyzer.java, InitializationPlan/InitializationDependency/InitializationCycle, callable and aggregate-related types, module graph structures, backend-runtime.md initialization rules, and the eager/callable counterexamples in Domain11SemanticTest.java. Brainstorm a bounded interprocedural execution/dependency model for direct, namespace, callable, higher-order parameter/result, array/tuple/projection, returned aggregate, and function-valued-element paths. Analyze strict left-to-right and source-order event selection, positional parameter bindings, persistent cell state after known calls, closure-captured mutation, legal function-only recursion, active-versus-completed recursion guards, and whether dependencies should follow only actual statically knowable invocation paths or every conservative path. Define a clean 11C boundary and contract with provenance/flow work, migration risks from the current walk, inputs/outputs, invariants, tests, and an independent cycle-detection gate; identify spec-required versus over-conservative behavior and any owner decisions. Do not edit implementation or duplicate the general provenance architecture role.

roles.name: Language Contract, Phase Boundaries, and Red-Team Recovery
roles.lens: Act as the specification-alignment and recovery/red-team domain, centered on concern D while adjudicating the whole phase-11 decomposition. Read .internal-dev/specifications/language-core.md, backend-runtime.md, the phase-11 plan/changelog/knowledge records, TypedSemanticProvenance.java, TypedSemanticGraph.java, IrValidator.java, TypedIrBuilder.java, and the relevant conditional, tuple-root, nil, and forged-graph tests. Classify validator findings as normative requirements, likely over-strict implementation behavior, genuine ambiguity requiring owner approval, or phase-12 IR-sealing concerns. Specifically examine tuple-root nested mutation versus non-assignable tuple fields, selected-member identity versus sibling taint, must-reject joins across reachable paths, contextual nil inference for then-only Unit conditionals and nested blocks/composites, and provenance that cannot trust forged published types. Compare 11A aggregate/callable provenance, 11B general flow state, 11C eager initialization, and 11D nil/contextual typing as independently gated boundaries; state what interfaces and evidence must be frozen before phase 12. Propose a counterexample matrix, regression and independent-validation sequence, migration/scope risks, and a distinct red-team synthesis protocol that preserves participating findings separately. Do not implement code, silently revise contracts, or broaden into backend/runtime/CLI or deferred features.
